title: Introduce invocation-ledger and sparse-token-sonic dashboard for fine-grained cost/latency attribution
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a new invocation ledger service for per-invocation token cost attribution, a sparse-token-sonic dashboard to visualize burst and cadence patterns, and lightweight alert knobs for long-tail token-cost regressions.
description: Motivation: Customers asked for a compact, queryable ledger that ties token-level cost and phase latencies to invocation metadata without exploding cardinality. This PR introduces an 'invocation-ledger' component that records per-invocation summarized phase timing, token counts per phase, model-variant fingerprints, and a compact cost estimate derived from kernel-duration tags. We also add a Sparsified Token Sonic dashboard that surfaces rhythmic burst patterns, cadence anomalies, and per-route cost hotlines so SREs and product engineers can triage cost spikes quickly. Changes: 1) New service: telemetry/invocation_ledger service written in Go (30 files, small runtime library) that consumes sampled spans and KV-cache hints, deduplicates by invocation fingerprint, and writes compact rows to the telemetry store. 2) Aggregation pipeline: a lightweight Rollup job that computes phase-level median/95/99 latency and cost-per-token for each model-version/route/timebin. 3) Dashboard: Grafana panels under Observability -> Invocation Ledger that show the sparse-token-sonic heatmap, per-phase stacked latency bars, and a per-invocation ledger explorer with linkable trace anchors. 4) Alerts: new alert rule 'InvocLedger:TokenCostLongTail' with hysteresis and quiet windows to reduce alert churn; defaults tuned conservatively. 5) Tests: unit tests for ledger dedupe and e2e replay harness for synthetic bursts. Backwards compatibility: ledger consumes existing span tags and adds no additional tags to production traces; rollup is opt-in via feature-flag 'telemetry.invocation_ledger.enabled'. Implementation notes: ledger rows are intentionally compact (single proto with short field IDs) to limit storage; we compute a conservative cost estimate using per-kernel-duration buckets and hardware-weight factors from existing HW tags. We do not change the public Redwood API surface. Performance: microbenchmarks show the ledger consumer can sustain 2x sampling throughput of our default sampling rate with <7% CPU on a c5.4xlarge equivalent; rollup job is memory-efficient due to tiling. Operational concerns: retention defaults to 30d for ledger rows and 7d for rollup aggregates to balance queryability and cost. Feature flag and RBAC gating added to console. See release notes for opt-in instructions.
